title: The spectrum at a glance
intro: Proposals are ordered from the end that gives the whole land to Israeli sovereignty and removes or disenfranchises Palestinians, through partition and shared arrangements, to the end that gives the whole land to a single state, ending with a Palestinian-ruled state that excludes or expels Jews. The ordering runs mainly along who holds sovereignty over which territory, and then along how political rights are distributed. It is a simplification: two-state, confederal and one-state models can each be built with very different security and rights terms.
caption: Ordering by the editors for game-design purposes. Placement describes each proposal's structure, not its merit, legality or likelihood; several proposals at both ends would involve serious violations of international law, as discussed in the relevant sections.

groups.name: Israeli sovereignty over all the land

models.name: Population transfer / "encouraged emigration"
models.gist: Palestinians leave the West Bank and/or Gaza, by agreement, incentive or force (Peel 1937 exchange idea, Moledet, post-2023 Gaza emigration schemes, the 2025 "Gaza Riviera").

models.name: Annexation without equal rights
models.gist: Israel annexes the territories. Palestinians get residency or local self-rule without a national vote (Smotrich's 2017 Decisive Plan).

models.name: Annexation with citizenship
models.gist: Israel annexes the West Bank and phases in citizenship for its Palestinians, usually excluding Gaza and refugee return (Glick, Elitzur, Hotovely, Rivlin).

models.name: Autonomy
models.gist: Self-government over people with sovereignty left open (the Allon Plan 1967, Begin 1977, the Camp David framework 1978).

models.name: Enclaves and emirates
models.gist: Israel annexes Area C or most of the West Bank; Palestinians govern city islands or clan-run "emirates" (Bennett 2012, Smotrich's 82% map, Kedar, the 2025 Hebron proposal).

models.name: Jordanian option
models.gist: Jordan takes responsibility for West Bank Palestinians (the London Agreement 1987, "Jordan is Palestine"). Jordan has rejected this since 1988.

models.name: Conflict management
models.gist: No final settlement: a security-led status quo, "shrinking the conflict", economic peace and regional normalisation around an unresolved core.

models.name: Three-state solution
models.gist: Gaza linked to Egypt and the West Bank to Jordan (Bolton 2009, Eiland's land swaps), or two separate Palestinian entities, as entrenched since 2007.

models.name: Conditional statehood (Trump 2020)
models.gist: A state with restricted sovereignty, Israeli control of the Jordan Valley and settlements, conditions judged by Israel and the US.

models.name: Negotiated two states
models.gist: The 1967 lines with roughly 2–7% swaps, Jerusalem divided by neighbourhood, a special regime for the holy sites, a non-militarised Palestine, and refugee return mainly to Palestine (Clinton, Taba, Geneva, Olmert, Kerry).

models.name: Regional and multilateral track
models.gist: Statehood paired with Arab normalisation and recognition from outside the region (the Arab Peace Initiative, the 2025 New York Declaration, about 157 recognitions).

models.name: Confederation
models.gist: Two sovereign states with open borders, residency separate from citizenship, and joint institutions (A Land for All; the Beilin–Husseini Holy Land Confederation).

models.name: Jordanian–Palestinian confederation
models.gist: A Palestinian state linked to Jordan. Amman accepts this only after statehood (the 1985 Hussein–Arafat accord, the 2018 revival).

models.name: Federation, cantons or parallel states
models.gist: One federal framework with ethnic or territorial units (canton plans; LeVine and Mossberg's "parallel states").

models.name: International trusteeship
models.gist: International administration of contested areas: the 1947 Jerusalem corpus separatum, a special regime for the Holy Basin, and the 2025 Board of Peace and stabilisation force for Gaza.

groups.name: One state over all the land

models.name: The one-state reality (baseline)
models.gist: A description of today, not a proposal: one power rules from the river to the sea with unequal rights (Lustick; Barnett, Brown, Lynch and Telhami). Every endgame departs from it.

models.name: Binational state
models.gist: Political parity between two nations in one polity (Brit Shalom, Ihud, the 1947 UNSCOP minority federal plan).

models.name: One democratic state with full return
models.gist: Equal citizenship with refugee return and restitution (Said, Judt, Abunimah, the One Democratic State Campaign).

models.name: Palestinian/Arab state with limited or no rights for Jews
models.gist: Palestinian sovereignty over all the land with Jewish presence limited or removed (the 1968 PLO Charter, the 1988 Hamas Charter, the 2021 "Promise of the Hereafter" conference).
